children: The earnings downgrade cycle for Nifty50 companies showed signs of easing in August, with 23 of the 50 index constituents, or 46%, seeing upgrades to their FY27 EPS estimates, led by cement, oil & gas, telecom, infrastructure and autos, according to JM Financial. Overall, FY27 EPS estimates for the Nifty50 edged up 0.1% month-on-month in August, reversing some of the weakness seen in July.
Earnings estimates show signs of stabilisation

According to the JM Financial report, the increase in August came after FY27 EPS estimates fell 0.7% month-on-month in July. FY28 EPS estimates also rose 0.2% in August, after declining 0.5% in July. The improvement, however, comes after a significant earnings reset over the past year. JM Financial said Nifty50 FY27 EPS estimates have been cut 9.3% between August 2025 and August 2026, while FY28 estimates have declined 7.5%. Over the same period, the Nifty50 has delivered a negative return of 1.4%.
Cement emerged as the biggest contributor to the improvement in earnings estimates in August. JM Financial said FY27 EPS estimates for the sector rose 9% month-on-month.
NBFCs followed with a 1.8% increase, while oil & gas and metals & mining saw 0.5% increases in FY27 EPS estimates.

The brokerage also found that upgrades were relatively broad-based across some sectors. Both oil & gas companies and both cement companies in the Nifty50 saw their FY27 EPS estimates upgraded. The index's lone telecom company also received an upgrade.
Infrastructure and ports saw upgrades in two of its three companies, while three of the five auto companies saw their FY27 EPS estimates raised.
At the stock level, Grasim, Bajaj Finserv, Hindalco, SBI and Titan recorded some of the biggest FY27 EPS upgrades in August, JM Financial said.

The earnings improvement was not broad-based, with some sectors still facing pressure. Consumer companies saw the sharpest cut in FY27 EPS estimates at 4.7% month-on-month, followed by automobiles at 2.2%, according to JM Financial.
At the individual stock level, ITC, Tata Steel, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Maruti Suzuki and Adani Enterprises saw some of the biggest cuts to their FY27 EPS estimates during the month.

Overall, 17 Nifty50 companies, or 34%, saw FY27 EPS downgrades in August. Metals & mining recorded the highest proportion of cuts, with three of its four Nifty50 companies seeing downgrades. Banks also remained under pressure, with three out of five companies seeing their FY27 EPS estimates cut.

title: Earnings downgrade ease: 46% of Nifty 50 stocks see FY27 EPS upgrades in August
